indicators.note: the pair is set down inside the word for plots, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: plots of land are sites

explanation.surface: A couple of garden gnomes are set out in the allotments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placed in' puts PR inside SITES, splitting it after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprites and gnomes are both small mischievous spirits of folklore.

clue.text: Distance covered by troops, cruel people

indicators.note: the troops wrap round the distance, so the abbreviation for distance goes inside

parts.note: the SAS is the British Army's Special Air Service regiment
DIST is the abbreviation for distance

explanation.surface: A distance marched by soldiers under brutal commanders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered by' puts DIST inside SAS after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: These are people who take pleasure in inflicting pain on others.

definitions.meaning: to esteem or value someone highly
a particular point, as in 'in every way'

explanation.surface: Value every particular.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem someone is to hold them in regard, and a particular point or aspect is a 'respect' in phrases like 'in that regard'.

indicators.note: the article sits inside the word for dye

parts.note: a tint is a dye or colouring
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An item of clothing is ruined in the dyeing.
explanation.definitionFit: To taint something is to contaminate or ruin it.

clue.text: Persuade to follow game, with very little time to enter

indicators.note: the small word and the time go inside the word for following game

parts.note: to stalk is to track game animals stealthily
wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: Someone coaxes a friend into joining a game with seconds to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' puts WEE and T inside STALK after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax with flattery is to win someone over by charming words.

clue.text: Sickly sweetness in form of claret produced by Spain

indicators.note: the wine is put into another form, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A wine merchant describes a cloying Spanish claret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in form of' rearranges CLARET to TREACL; E for Spain follows, as 'produced by' links the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, treacle is cloying sentimentality, a syrupy over-sweetness of manner.

definitions.meaning: someone who makes an effort, who keeps having a go
an ancient city on the Moselle in western Germany

explanation.surface: A man is having a hard time in a German city.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has a go is a striver, and the Roman-founded city on the Moselle in Germany has the same name.

clue.text: Character in City, almost loaded, investing cash

indicators.note: to invest is to clothe or surround, so the city and the trimmed word go round the cash

parts.note: EC is the postcode area for the City of London

indicators.note: almost means the word falls one letter short of its end

parts.note: someone loaded is rich
a cent is a coin, a small piece of cash

explanation.surface: A City trader, nearly rich, is putting money into the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims RICH to RIC, and 'investing' wraps EC + RIC round CENT. Loaded means wealthy; investing means surrounding. A 'character' is an odd person.
explanation.definitionFit: A character is someone odd or quirky, an oddball.

clue.text: Choral work shows piety at start of Advent

parts.note: cant is hypocritical pious talk

indicators.note: the start of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A church choir piece shows devotion as the Advent season begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' takes the first letter of 'Advent'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a sung composition for voices and instruments, often sacred.

indicators.note: the queen is set into the rearranged letters like a jewel
the medal is redesigned, so its letters take a new arrangement

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: A medal is newly designed with a portrait of the Queen inlaid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges MEDAL to EMALD, and 'inlaid' sets ER in after EM.
explanation.definitionFit: A green gemstone is an ornament, worn as jewellery or set as a decoration.

clue.text: Son (mine) seen plunging into river, notwithstanding?

indicators.note: the son and the mine dive into the river, so they go inside its name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales, a crossword favourite
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A son down the mine is pictured diving into a river regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plunging into' puts S and PIT between the first two letters of DEE and the last.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are prepositions meaning in spite of something.

parts.note: a fire that is still in is still burning

indicators.note: what is reported is heard, so the word for divine is given by its sound

parts.note: to divine something is to sense it

explanation.surface: Someone ablaze with holy zeal, it is said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' turns SENSE into its sound-alike CENSE. 'Burning' looks like part of a church picture of smoking censers but gives IN; the definition is 'fire' as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire someone up, or inflame them, is to make them furious, as to incense means to enrage.

definitions.meaning: a fan at a match watches from the stands
A long-running British weekly political magazine

explanation.surface: A football supporter's favourite periodical.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan at a game is an onlooker in the crowd, and the weekly of that name is a British current-affairs title.

indicators.note: the animal is formed of letters taken from inside the next two words

explanation.surface: A quiz asks whether a creature of Kenya might be a langur monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' points to the letters running across 'keNYA LAngur'. A langur is an Asian monkey, a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned antelope of southern Africa.

indicators.note: here 'on' means coming next to, so the short name is attached after the word for settle

parts.note: to settle into a chair is to sit
Ed is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Little Edward was put down on a wooden bench.
explanation.walkthrough: A settle is also an old high-backed wooden bench, which the surface uses; here it is the verb meaning sit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sited has been positioned or located in a particular spot.

clue.text: Religious title, one accepted by Peruvian monk

parts.note: Dom is a title given to some monks

indicators.note: the one is taken in by the Peruvian, so it goes inside

parts.note: the Incan Empire was centred on Peru
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Peruvian monk is given a religious title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted by' puts I inside INCAN after IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A friar of the order founded by St Dominic is often called a Black Friar.

parts.note: the symbol meaning 'and' is in effect a sign for 'plus' as well

explanation.definitionFit: The & symbol stands for 'and', which in arithmetic talk means plus.

clue.text: It's for each Spartan to soldier on

parts.note: per means for each, as in 'per head'
Spartan means austere, harsh

explanation.surface: Each Spartan warrior must fight on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spartan' suggests the warriors of ancient Sparta but means austere.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going despite difficulty is to carry on, as a soldier keeps fighting.

clue.text: Type open to a better printer?

definitions.text: Type open to a better printer?

parts.words: Type open to a better printer?
parts.note: read as a person who takes bets from any punter, but also as a printer, a maker of volumes

explanation.surface: A typeface that might suit a superior printing house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' is a kind of person, and the 'better' is someone betting; a maker of books could also be a printer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookie accepts wagers from punters, and literally a maker of books is a printer or publisher.

indicators.note: the worry goes about the rook, enclosing it

parts.note: to bother is to worry
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess player frets over a rook as checkmate approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R inside BOTHER after the B. 'mate' suggests checkmate but means a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pal or comrade is often hailed as a sibling.

parts.note: something on and going is both working and continuing without a break

explanation.surface: A machine that keeps running while switched on.
explanation.definitionFit: Something continuing without a pause carries on, as a machine runs while switched on.

clue.text: Renounces origins by word of mouth

indicators.note: a thing passed by word of mouth is spoken, so the word for origins is taken by sound

parts.note: seeds are the origins from which things grow

explanation.surface: Someone abandons their roots in conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up a claim or territory is to yield it formally to another.

indicators.note: sparkling letters are fizzing about, so the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cleaning product leaves a grid sparkling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sparkling' looks like the result of the cleaning but signals the rearrangement of HAS GRID.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth for washing the dishes is a tool for cleaning up.

clue.text: Was unfaithful, upsetting steady relationship initially

indicators.note: the steady pair is upset, so these letters are tipped into a new order
initially takes just the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Someone cheated, wrecking a steady relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives R, the first letter of 'relationship', and 'upsetting' rearranges it with STEADY.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to wander from a partner, to have an affair.

definitions.meaning: a newspaper that speaks for a party is its official voice
a keyboard instrument with pipes, found in churches

explanation.surface: A musician asks for a replacement mouthpiece.
explanation.definitionFit: A party's official newspaper is its voice or medium, and the pipe-and-keyboard church instrument shares the name.

clue.text: Take new course in public relations? Sign of things to come

indicators.note: the take and the new course sit inside the abbreviation for public relations

parts.note: R stands for recipe, Latin for take, on prescriptions

indicators.note: a new course is the same letters given a fresh order

explanation.surface: A firm decides to change direction in its PR, a hint of what is ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges COURSE to ECURSO; R goes before it and 'in' places RECURSO between the P and R of PR.
explanation.definitionFit: A forerunner is something that comes before and heralds what follows.

clue.text: Botanical feature made by Prince and others

parts.note: et al is Latin for 'and others'

explanation.surface: A garden feature created by a prince and his staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A coloured leaflike part of a flower is a part a botanist studies.

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article
der is the German definite article

explanation.surface: A survey of European goods finds them second-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' looks like goods but means grammatical words: UN from French, DER from German.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lower in rank or quality sits beneath, as in 'the underdog'.

clue.text: A rich developing state, in trim

indicators.note: something developing is changing shape, so the letters of the two words are reorganised

parts.note: UT is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Utah

explanation.surface: A wealthy emerging nation is said to be in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' rearranges A RICH to HAIRC, and UT follows; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A trim is a light cut of the hair.

parts.note: the elder is a small tree bearing elderberries

indicators.note: a gutted word has lost its insides, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An aged tree has fallen with its trunk hollowed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' removes the middle of LAY, leaving its first and last letters L and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An elderly person is advanced in years, aged.

clue.text: Trap concealed by material on the Queen's side?

indicators.note: the trap is hidden inside the word for material, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: material things are real and tangible
a gin is a snare for catching game

explanation.surface: A snare hidden in fabric is placed by a royal supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like cloth but means real; 'concealed by' puts GIN inside REAL after RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Regina is Latin for queen, so the adjective means relating to a queen, belonging to her side.

indicators.note: letters up in arms are in turmoil, so the nobleman's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grand nobleman is furious and protesting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up in arms' means protesting angrily and also signals the rearrangement of GRANDEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being enraged is being furious, wild with temper.
